round2.why: Record CLM-001 AR phone: V keeps the whole title in one Arabic sans family on three lines, while W sets 'Global Findex 2021' in a Latin serif on its own fourth line (and the Payments AR title grows to four lines), which reads as a heading imported from the English page and pushes the first sentence of the answer further down the phone screen; W's serif gains distinctiveness only on the English desktop views, which this reader rarely sees.

weight.why: At 30px on a phone the 600 weight keeps the counters and the diacritics of 'الأجهزة المُبلَّغ عنها' and the dots of 'القياس' open while still standing clearly apart from the regular body; the 700 weight clots those strokes and makes the Latin 'Global Findex 2021' line heavier than its Arabic neighbours, buying distinction the 600 already has.

round2.why: V keeps the same first-screen economy as W on Home EN desktop but its Arabic pages are set in one face throughout, whereas on Record CLM-001 AR phone W drops the English serif into the Arabic title for 'Global Findex 2021' and on Home AR phone promotes the summary sentence to a bold pull-quote that outranks its own heading, both signs of a composition mirrored from English rather than designed in Arabic.

W's serif display earns a more journal-like English page (Home EN desktop), but on the Record CLM-001 AR phone view the serif Latin 'Global Findex 2021' line sits inside an otherwise unchanged bold Arabic sans heading, so the Arabic reads as an English decision mirrored over rather than designed, whereas V keeps one coherent type system across both languages with the same provenance block, measure and navigation.
